title: Trump and Putin hold first publicly confirmed phone call of Trump's second term
body:
On 12 February 2025, US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin held a telephone call lasting about an hour and a half. It was the first direct exchange between the two leaders since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Trump described it on Truth Social as lengthy and very productive and said the two had discussed Ukraine, the Middle East, energy, artificial intelligence and the strength of the dollar. He announced that negotiations to end the fighting would begin immediately.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed the call. He said Putin had stressed the need to address the root causes of the conflict, and that the two leaders had exchanged invitations to visit each other's countries. Trump also spoke with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky after the call and shared details of it.

The call followed a trip by US envoy Steve Witkoff to Moscow on 11 February to arrange the exchange of the American Marc Fogel for the Russian Alexander Vinnik. On the same day as the call, US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth told a meeting at NATO headquarters in Brussels that Ukrainian NATO membership was unlikely and that a return to Ukraine's pre-war borders was unrealistic. He later said that seeking peace was not a betrayal of Ukraine.

Bloomberg reported that European officials received no advance notice of the call. Foreign ministers from Ukraine, France, Germany, the United Kingdom, Italy, Spain and Poland, together with the head of the EU's foreign service, met in Paris and insisted that the EU must take part in negotiations. On 18 February, US delegates led by Secretary of State Marco Rubio met Russian delegates led by Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov in Saudi Arabia.
